newsitem.title: UK: Copper Creek mine construction to start in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Copper Creek mine construction to start in 1997.

text.p: AMT International Mining Corp of Canada said construction of its Copper Creek mine in Arizona will start in early 1997 with production on stream a year later, reaching 100 million pounds of copper (45,300 tonnes) and 100,000 ounces of gold equivalent by the year 2000.
The property was acquired for exploration under agreement from Magma Copper, now part of BHP Copper in 1993.
"I would suggest to you they wish we did not have it," AMT's chief operating officer, Glen Zinn joked at an analysts' briefing on Thursday.

Once the feasibility study is completed, BHP and AMT will both have a 50 percent stake in Copper Creek, but AMT has an option to acquire half of BHP's 50 percent stake. "I think we will exercise that," AMT's president and chief executive officer Kushal Singh told Reuters after the briefing.

Zinn claimed AMT's share price was undervalued because proven, probable and drilled metal reserves per share equalled 150 pounds of copper, 3 pounds of molybdenum and 1.6 grams of gold. The combined metal value was $200 per share at current prices, Zinn calculated.
AMT's share traded Thursday at C$1.25 per share, off 7 cents.
Singh said it will cost C$11.5 million to complete the feasibility studies for a two standalone projects - oxide ore mining and leaching, and sulphide ore underground mining.

A further US$10 million will be needed to bring the leaching project on stream, producing 15 million pounds of copper a year, and $35 to $40 million to start up the sulphide project producing 100 million pounds eventually.
"I don't see any reason why we would have difficulty in the financing," Singh said.
AMT will sell the leached copper in crystal form to BHP Copper who will then process it into cathode at the San Manuel smelter just 12 miles from Copper Creek.
The company is negotiating with BHP to toll Copper Creek's sulphide ore into copper at San Manuel.

AMT has tentative permission to start constructing two sulphide declines in early 1997. Zinn said cash costs for copper production will be 50 cents per pound or below and "will probably be in the 40 cents range".
Copper Creek has 10 million tonnes of proven and probably reserves grading over 2 percent copper, and an additional six million tonnes of ore grading 0.8 percent copper for leaching, Singh said.

AMT has a 51 percent stake in a venture to explore the Copper Prince and Globe properties contiguous to Copper Creek. Phelps Dodge Corp owns the properties and has the remaining 49 percent stake in the venture.
AMT's initial public offering in March raised C$6.5 million. and a second offering in May raised C$3 million. On a fully diluted basis there are 28.3 million shares.

Of the fully diluted total, 17.1 million shares are outstanding, and management holds options on 1 to 2 million shares. Additionally there are over 9 million share warrants that have to be exercised by March next year.
